headline: GOLD HOLDS $3,950 WHILE SILVER CRASHES 3.3% — Iran Strikes and Midterm Uncertainty Split Precious Metals on Election Night
snippet: Gold edged higher as a safe-haven bid held while silver fell sharply on election day, with fresh U.S. strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure drawing an unusual split between the two metals. Silver tracked risk assets lower while gold absorbed defensive flows from investors unwilling to step out of bullion ahead of potentially market-moving vote results.

headline: RIO TINTO COMMISSIONS TWO MORE LITHIUM PROJECTS IN CATAMARCA — A$1.4B Argentina Buildout Hits Major Milestone
snippet: Rio Tinto officially commissioned two additional lithium projects in Argentina's Catamarca province today, bringing its total Argentine lithium investment to approximately US$1.4 billion across three provinces. The expansion adds to the company's flagship Rincón lithium project in Salta, cementing Rio Tinto's position as a major non-Chinese battery metals supplier.

headline: $712 BILLION ERASED FROM MINING GIANTS SINCE IRAN WAR BEGAN — Sector Losses Now Match a Full 2008 Financial Crisis
snippet: The world's 50 largest mining companies have collectively shed $712 billion in market capitalisation since the start of the Iran war, with oil price volatility, supply chain disruption, and sustained risk-off positioning hitting miners across all commodities. The sector posted its worst two-month equity decline since 2008 through October.

headline: BUNKER HILL + SILVER47 MERGE NOVEMBER 5 — Both Shareholder Votes Approved; $163M U.S. Silver Platform Goes Live Next Week
snippet: Shareholders of both Bunker Hill Mining and Silver47 approved their $163 million all-stock business combination on October 27–28, with closing expected November 5 pending final court and stock exchange approvals. The merged Idaho-focused entity also secured $20 million in new capital to fund the Bunker Hill mine ramp-up toward year-end commercial production.

headline: DRC SEIZES COPPER AND COBALT AT LUALABA ILLEGAL MINING SITES — Supply-Chain Risk Escalates in World's Top Cobalt Province
snippet: Congolese authorities seized copper and cobalt at multiple illegal mining sites including Menda in Lualaba province, escalating enforcement in the DRC's most productive mining corridor. Artisanal and illegal mining accounts for a significant share of DRC cobalt output, giving crackdowns direct implications for battery metal supply chains.

headline: HUDBAY LEADS C$49.8M RAISE FOR PECOY COPPER'S PERU PROJECT — Senior Producer Backs Junior Discovery as Copper Demand Outlook Improves
snippet: Hudbay Minerals is leading a C$49.8 million private placement in Pecoy Copper to advance its copper exploration project in Peru, signalling continued senior-producer appetite for strategic stakes in early-stage discoveries even as junior valuations remain broadly depressed across the sector.

headline: COPPERCORP GETS TASMANIA GOVT DRILL GRANT — Final Jukes Hole 12m @ 0.54% Cu Closes Skyline Program at Razorback
snippet: CopperCorp Resources concluded its Jukes Skyline drill program at the Razorback copper-gold-REE property in western Tasmania with hole JDD008 returning 12.0 m @ 0.54% Cu, 0.14 g/t Au, and 0.89 g/t Ag. Simultaneously, the Tasmanian government awarded an EDGI co-funding grant to support the Phase 2 drill program, reducing cash requirements for the next campaign.

headline: ENERGY FUELS BUILDS U.S. RARE EARTH HUB AT UTAH'S WHITE MESA MILL — Uranium Operation Pivots to Challenge China's Supply Lock
snippet: Energy Fuels is expanding its White Mesa Mill in Utah into a rare earth separation and processing hub alongside existing uranium production, aiming to provide the U.S. and allied countries with a non-Chinese source of neodymium, praseodymium, and heavy rare earths for defence and EV motor magnets. Executives say the dual-use facility model lowers capital intensity compared to a greenfield rare earth plant.

headline: SILVER AT $48.96 ON ELECTION DAY: Will Post-Midterm Stability Relaunch the Rally Toward $55?
snippet: With silver declining 3.3% to $48.96 on election day amid macro uncertainty, analysts are watching for post-midterm stabilisation to re-establish the metal's industrial and monetary demand bid. The $50 level is cited as the key inflection point for renewed bullish momentum, with the outcome of rate expectations and any post-election fiscal clarity seen as the main drivers.

headline: 5 CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH THIS NOVEMBER — Q3 Earnings Season Opens as Gold Tests $4,000 Floor
snippet: IAMGOLD, Barrick, and three other major Canadian gold producers are scheduled to report Q3 results in the next 10 days, with the sector down 26% from its February 2026 peak even as spot gold holds near $4,000. Production volumes, all-in sustaining costs, and any guidance revisions are expected to act as the primary catalysts for moves in the individual names.
